summary: Thoroughly tested the new WAS-price sale mode end-to-end: backend bulk-sale-pricing endpoint (explicit WAS + legacy % + clear_sale + low-WAS rejection), storefront guest flow (LP-1214 Dolomite Onyx Green/Polished/60x120cm), storefront trade flow, and admin bulk Sale/Labels modal (WAS default mode, % switch, data-testids). All flows PASS. LP-1214 left on sale as instructed.

cases: TestLegacyDiscountPercentMode::test_legacy_apply_and_clear — legacy {discount_percentage:10} works: was=price, now=price*0.9, then clear_sale removes all sale fields; price untouched
TestExplicitWasRejectLowWas::test_low_was_rejected — WAS below current price returns updated_count=0 with 'must be higher' error
TestExplicitWasSetAndClear::test_explicit_was_flow_with_tiles_mirror — explicit WAS sets was_price, now_price=price, price unchanged, derived % correct; tiles doc mirrored; cleanup clear performed

storefront_guest_LP1214.1m2: SALE ribbon (data-testid=sale-price-ribbon) shows WAS £39.99, NOW £30.00, SAVE £9.99, 25% OFF — matches expected
storefront_guest_LP1214.15m2: NOW £28.50, SAVE £11.49, 29% OFF; breakdown rows: 'Sale: 25% off | Volume: 4% off | Total: 29% off' — sale+volume compounding correct
storefront_guest_LP1214.regression: Non-sale variant (Bianco/Matt/120x120cm) shows plain £30.00 with NO sale ribbon; Volume Pricing table still renders

storefront_trade.login: trade.test@tilestation.co.uk logged in, header switched to 'Trade Tester'
storefront_trade.1m2: WAS £33.33 (ex VAT), NOW £23.75, SAVE £9.58, 29% OFF; breakdown 'Sale: 25% off | Trade: 4% off | Total: 29% off'; '+ Extra 2% Credit Back' shown
storefront_trade.15m2: NOW £22.56, 32% OFF; breakdown 'Sale: 25% off | Volume: 4% off | Trade: 3% off | Total: 32% off'; total % OFF (32%) > guest 15m² (29%) as expected
storefront_trade.logout: Trade row absent for guests (verified in earlier guest run before login)

admin_bulk_sale_modal.opened: Bulk Sale & Labels modal opened on 2 selected products
admin_bulk_sale_modal.apply_discount_toggle: Enabling 'Apply discount to all selected products' reveals mode buttons and red explanation box: 'Your list price stays exactly as it is. The storefront shows WAS £54.99 with the current price in bold red as the SALE price...'
admin_bulk_sale_modal.default_mode: 'Set WAS price (£)' is DEFAULT (red highlighted); data-testid='sale-mode-was' present
admin_bulk_sale_modal.percent_mode_switch: Clicking data-testid='sale-mode-percent' reveals data-testid='bulk-discount-percent-input' (visible=true); switching back to WAS restores WAS input
admin_bulk_sale_modal.not_applied: Did NOT dispatch a WAS apply from the modal to avoid polluting real products; the backend explicit-WAS branch (which the modal calls) is fully covered by pytest test_explicit_was_flow_with_tiles_mirror

critical_code_review_comments: supplier_sync.py file is very large (>7500 lines) — recommend splitting into route modules (products, sale-pricing, tiers, sync) for maintainability.
Explicit-WAS branch and legacy branch live in the same endpoint; consider clear docstring or splitting to prevent future duplicate-Pydantic-class regressions like the one just fixed.
